goal: Nan, a five-year-old girl with large dark-brown eyes, short black hair in two small bunches, an orange T-shirt with a white star, red shorts, and white sneakers, holds up a big sheet of paper painted all orange at an easel in the art corner of the kindergarten classroom. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows the girl Nan (the approved 3D character; ignore the dog next to her, it must not appear unless the page names Pip). Picture 2 is a close-up of Nan's face with the correct, clean eyes: copy her face and eyes from it exactly; each eye ends in a smooth, rounded outer corner with one short, thick, curved eyelash flick; there is no pale skin flap, no torn edge, and no separate small tick mark at any eye corner. Picture 3 is the empty art corner of the kindergarten classroom: cream plaster walls with dark-brown timber beams, a wooden plank floor, a small window, two wooden easels with blank paper, and a low wooden table with paint pots; use it as the background and keep the same room. Picture 4 shows seven thin sheets of paper, each painted all over in one flat color: red, blue, yellow, green (top row), orange, pink, purple (bottom row); draw only the one sheet this picture needs, as a thin, flat sheet of paper. Picture 5 shows one child-height wooden easel with a blank sheet of paper and three paint pots on its ledge. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Nan: black-brown hair in exactly two round buns with smooth red ring bands (no bun on top), large dark-brown eyes, an orange T-shirt with a white star, red shorts, white sneakers. The picture: Nan holds up a big sheet of orange paper at an easel. A medium shot at a low camera height. Nan stands next to the right easel of the art corner (picture 3; one easel as in picture 5, with a blank sheet on it), faces the camera, smiles, and holds up one big thin sheet of paper painted all ORANGE (the orange sheet of picture 4; draw only that one sheet) in front of her chest with both hands, five short fingers visible at its edges. The whole sheet is in view, flat, plain orange, with no marks. The art corner is soft behind her. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "It is orange." and is context only: do not draw any text. Nan's face must match her close-up: the same wide round chibi face, the same big brown irises with two white highlights, the same small nose and eyebrows; do not change her hair, eyes, or clothes.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the star. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, two or three big closed beam shapes, the window as one closed square, each easel as one closed frame, the table as one closed shape, the toy kitchen and the shelf as large closed box shapes). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no plaster texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details on the shelf. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Nan keeps her painted eyelash mark in the line art: at the outer corner of each visible eye, draw ONE short thick solid stroke (as thick as the outline) that touches the eye outline. The eyelash stroke is the only mark beside each eye. Each hair bun is one closed circle with its red band as one closed strip. Each painted sheet of paper is one closed rectangle with nothing drawn inside it (the paint color is not drawn).
